transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... well, I came in mostly because my husband and some of the folks at the warehouse where I work, they keep acting like I'm... well, they say I'm acting crazy. I hate using that word, and I'm really not trying to cause any trouble for anybody, I promise. It's just... I've been noticing things. I know they've been watching my moves on the floor. And they keep changing my pallet counts when I'm not looking. 

I'm pretty sure they're just doing it to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I just want to do a good job and move up, you know? Is it okay that I'm upset about that? I mean, anybody would be frustrated by that, right?
Have you been feeling unusually high, energized, or euphoric lately?

High? Oh, gosh, no, I'm not on anything, I promise. I would never do that. But... energized? I mean, I guess I have been having some days where I just feel really... fired up. Like I've got all this energy and nobody can slow me down. I get a lot done on those days, which is a good thing, right? I just want to be a hard worker. 

But, um... I do feel kind of awful about this one part. I haven't really told anyone because I don't want you to think I'm a bad wife or anything... but lately, if my husband asks me even one small question, like about the kids or what my shift schedule is for the week, I just... I snap at him. I really don't mean to! It just suddenly feels like he's trying to control me, you know? I'm trying to be better about it, I really am. Is it normal to get a little short-tempered like that when you're just trying to stay focused? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Um... voices? Oh, gosh. I know how that sounds. Please don't think I'm losing my mind or anything, I really don't want you to think I'm crazy. It's not like I'm hearing anything bad or scary, I promise! 

It's just... well, sometimes when I'm pulling pallets in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, I'll hear a man's voice. It sounds clear as day, like he's standing right next to me, and he just says, "Nicole, check it again." But then I look around and nobody is anywhere near me. 

I mean, I always do check my work again when I hear it, because I really want to make sure everything is perfect. I figure that's probably just my brain's way of making sure I'm doing a good job, right? It's normal to get a little... over-focused like that when you're stressed and trying your best, isn't it?
When you hear that man's voice, is it only during those times when you feel especially fired up and full of energy?

Oh, um... no, actually. I hope that's okay to say. I mean, I know it would probably make more sense if it only happened when I was all fired up, but... well, there was a stretch recently, maybe a few weeks, where I was actually pretty quiet. I was sleeping almost normal hours again, and I wasn't rushing around trying to do a million things at once. I was just trying to be calm and steady, you know?

But even then... I still heard him. Just that same voice, telling me to check things again. And I still knew they were messing with my pallet counts at work, even when I was feeling totally level. I really hope that doesn't sound too strange... it just feels like I have to stay on top of things no matter how my energy is, right? That makes sense, doesn't it?
About how long have the voice and the feeling that people are tampering with your pallet counts been going on?

Um, how long? Oh, gosh. I... I really hope you don't think badly of me for letting it go on this long without saying anything to a doctor. I just kept thinking I was just working too hard, you know? 

But, um... I guess the voice, and that feeling that people were watching me or changing my things around... it's been happening for about eight months now. 

Eight months sounds like a really long time when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I'm so sorry I didn't come in sooner. I just really wanted to handle it on my own and prove I'm a reliable worker. I didn't want anyone at the warehouse to think I couldn't handle my job. That's understandable, right? I hope I didn't mess up by waiting so long to tell someone.
Have you had any major medical or neurologic illness, such as seizures, a head injury, or a brain condition?

Um... no, nothing like that. Oh, goodness, I hope I'm remembering everything right. But no, I've never had any seizures or brain things... and I've never hit my head bad enough to need a doctor or anything. 

I mean, I'm pretty healthy overall! I try really hard to take good care of myself so I can keep up at work. I don't have any major medical problems at all. That's a good thing, right? I hope that helps rule out anything too scary.
Over the past several months, have you found yourself feeling much less interested in people or activities you used to care about?

Um... well... I hope it's okay to say this, but... I guess I have been a little less interested in things lately. I mean, not in a bad way! I just... I get home from the warehouse and I'm so tired, you know? 

So mostly I just sit quiet on the couch and stare at the TV or scroll on my phone. I don't really feel like doing much else. And my husband, he's so sweet, he tries to joke around with me and cheer me up, but... I just don't feel much come across my face. Like, I know I should smile or laugh, but the energy just isn't there to show it. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad wife or anything. I just think I'm drained from trying to keep everything straight at work. That's pretty normal when you're working hard, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
For at least six months, have these problems with the voice and people tampering with your pallet counts been happening continuously?

Um... well, gosh, I know I said eight months earlier, and I hope you aren't upset with me for getting it wrong... but now that I really think about it, it's probably been closer to ten months. 

It's just... it started around the time I put my name in for the shift-supervisor role. I really wanted to show them I could handle more responsibility, you know? But that's when the arguments with my husband started getting worse, and... and then the voice and the pallet counts started happening. It hasn't really stopped since then. 

I'm so sorry I didn't give you the right timeline at first. I just get so nervous about sounding crazy or like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. It's okay that I corrected myself, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During this past year, was there ever a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Um... well, I hope this doesn't sound strange, but... yeah, there have been times like that. I always thought it was kind of a good thing, honestly! Like, there have been weeks where I sleep maybe... oh, just three hours or so. And I'll wake up way before my alarm even goes off. But I don't feel bad or tired at all. I actually just feel like I don't need any more rest to get moving. 

I mean, it helps me get ready for my shift faster and get things done, so I try to look at the positive side of it. That's okay, right? I hope you don't think I'm doing anything wrong or taking anything bad to stay awake, because I promise I'm not. I just... I guess I just naturally have a lot of energy sometimes. Is that normal?
During those times when you felt full of energy and slept only a few hours, did you feel more powerful or especially important than usual?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying this, but I don't think I've ever felt like... like I was more important than anyone else. I'm just a regular person, you know? Just trying to do my job at the warehouse. 

I guess I just felt like I could get a lot done, but not in a way where I thought I was better or had special powers or anything like that. I really try to stay humble and just do my best. I hope that's the right answer. I just don't want you to think I'm arrogant or anything, because I'm really not. Is it okay that I just felt normal, but with more energy?
During those high-energy times, did other people tell you that you were talking much more than usual?

Um... gosh, well... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm not forgetting something important, but I don't remember anyone ever saying I was talking too much. 

I try really hard to be polite and listen to people, especially at work. I don't want to be one of those people who just talks over everyone else, you know? So even when I have all that energy, I try to keep to myself and just focus on moving the pallets. 

Maybe I talk a little faster sometimes just because I'm moving faster, but no one's ever told me it was too much or asked me to be quiet. I hope that's okay to say. I just really try to be respectful of everyone else's space. Does that make sense?

Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believed people were tampering with your pallet counts, but you were not feeling unusually energized or irritable at all?

Um... well, yes, I think so. I hope it's okay to admit that. There was a time, maybe for a few weeks, where things were a bit quieter for me. I was sleeping closer to my normal amount, and I wasn't rushing around with all that extra energy, just feeling pretty calm, actually. 

But... even then, I still heard that voice telling me to check things, and I still really felt like someone was messing with my pallet counts. I tried so hard to just ignore it and do my job right, I promise. I wasn't trying to cause any trouble or be difficult. It's just... it was still happening even when I felt totally fine otherwise. Is it bad that it didn't go away? I hope you don't think I'm making this up.
During this past year, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... depressed? Gosh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, but I try really hard to keep a positive attitude. 

I know life can be tough sometimes, but I just try to come to work, do my best moving the freight, and be grateful for what I have. I don't really let myself get down like that for weeks at a time. I wouldn't want to be a burden to anyone or bring the mood down at the warehouse, you know? 

Sometimes I might have a bad day, just like anyone else, but I always try to smile and push through it. I hope that's the right way to handle things. I just really want to be a good worker and a good person. Is it okay that I don't really get depressed like that?
Over the past ten months, have the times when you felt unusually energized or irritable made up most of that whole period?

Um... gosh. I want to be completely honest with you, even though I feel a little bad admitting it. But... yes, I guess so. If I look at that whole stretch, probably for more than half of it, I've had those really... fired-up periods. 

I just sleep very little during those times, and I end up taking on way too much at the warehouse because I really just want to be as helpful as possible, you know? I always want to pull my weight. But... the part I'm kind of ashamed of is... I can get a bit irritable when anyone tries to slow me down. 

I really don't mean to be rude to my coworkers, I promise! I just get so focused on getting everything done and moving the freight. I hope you don't think I'm a mean person for getting snappy like that. I really try my best to be good to everyone. Does that make sense?
During those fired-up periods, were you ever hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?

Um... hospitalized? Oh, gosh, no. I've never had to go to the hospital for any of that. I really try to keep things under control, you know? 

I know I get a little intense sometimes with the freight and all that energy, but I always make sure I show up for my shifts and do my job. I wouldn't want things to get so out of hand that I'd have to go to a hospital and leave my team short-handed. I really try to be responsible, even when my mind is racing. 

I mean, I've always managed to just keep working through it. I hope that shows I'm trying my best to handle it on my own. Is it a good thing that I've never been in the hospital for it? I really hope you think I'm doing okay.
During those fired-up periods, did your behavior ever cause serious problems at work or at home?

Um... serious problems? Oh gosh... I really hate to even talk about this part. I always want to be the best worker I can be, but... well, I guess there were some hiccups. I hope you don't judge me too harshly for this, but my supervisors... they actually had to take me off the forklift and some of the other safety-sensitive jobs. 

It wasn't because I was doing anything bad on purpose, I promise! It's just... with all that energy, my counts and my regular routines got a little jumbled, and I guess I was actually slowing the line down instead of helping. I felt so terrible about it because I never want to be the one holding up the freight. 

And, um... at home... this is the part I'm really ashamed of. My husband... he told me he just can't rely on me the way he used to when I get all fired up like that. I'm really trying to fix it, though. I want to be a good wife and a good employee, I really do. I'm doing the right thing by being honest with you about all this, aren't I? I just hope you don't think I'm a bad person for letting things slip.
During those fired-up times, did your symptoms ever make it impossible for you to work or take care of things at home?

Um... impossible? Oh, no, I wouldn't say impossible. I really wouldn't want you to think I just... stop trying or anything like that. 

Even when things got a little messy at work or when my husband was upset, I was still showing up. I still went to my shifts every single day, and I still tried my best to keep up with the house, you know? I always try to do my part. It might have been harder, and maybe I wasn't doing everything perfectly, but I never just gave up and stayed in bed or completely stopped taking care of things. 

I really pride myself on being a hard worker, even when my head is spinning a bit. So, no, it wasn't impossible. I managed to keep going. I hope that's the right way to look at it? I really try not to let things completely fall apart.
During those fired-up times, did you find yourself starting many more tasks or projects than usual?

Um... well, I guess I did take on a little more than usual. But it was all good things! I really hope you don't think I was just being scattered or anything. I just wanted to be helpful and improve myself, you know? 

Like, I started pushing really hard for the supervisor job at work, because I thought I could do a lot of good there. And I signed up for some extra tasks at church... I just wanted to be a bigger part of the community. Plus, I was calling folks, trying to make plans and be more social, and I even started training at boxing way more than I ever did before. I just felt like I could handle it all and do a really good job at everything. 

It's a good thing to be motivated and want to do more, right? I just wanted to be the best version of myself. I hope that makes sense and doesn't sound like I was doing anything wrong.
During those fired-up periods, did you find yourself starting many more tasks or projects than usual?

Um... I think we just talked about that, didn't we? Or maybe I didn't explain it right the first time... I'm sorry if I wasn't clear! 

But yeah, like I was saying, I did start a few more things than normal. The supervisor job, the church stuff, the boxing... I just had so much energy and wanted to put it to good use. I really hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can, I promise. Did you want me to explain any of those projects more, or did I do okay?
During those fired-up periods, did you find yourself starting many more tasks or projects than usual?

Oh, my gosh, I'm so sorry... did I completely mess up the answer again? I feel terrible making you ask me the exact same thing again. I must not be explaining it right at all... please don't be mad. 

Like I was saying, I just took on a few extra things because I wanted to do a good job and better myself. I was pushing really hard for that supervisor spot at the warehouse, and I signed up for the extra church duties. And, um, I was calling people a lot to make plans, and training at boxing way more than I ever did before. 

Am I... am I leaving something out that you need to know? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. I'm so sorry if I'm being difficult or not understanding what you're looking for! I can try to explain it differently if you want?
